Source and attribution

The archive attributes this English wording to Cours de philosophie positive (formula) and files it under Positivism. That locator distinguishes the passage from loose internet attributions: readers can return to the named work or section to check translation, surrounding argument, and edition-specific wording.

About Auguste Comte

Auguste Comte (1798–1857) was the French founder of positivism and an early systematizer of sociology. Once secretary to Saint-Simon, he later built an independent course of positive philosophy.

How to read this passage

Epistemology asks whether knowledge is justified true belief, reliable tracking of the world, or something else; it also asks how perception, testimony, memory, and reason contribute. This passage enters that discussion through knowledge, action.

Concepts in this quote

Knowledge
Knowledge is the philosophical study of what we can justifiably claim to know—and where certainty ends.
Action
Action concerns agency: what it is to do something intentionally, and how thought becomes practice.
